title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This is not a 1975–76 note on the divided-power de Rham complex. It is a recycled typescript page, upside down: page 160 of Grothendieck's Exposé IX of SGA 7 I, 'Modèles de Néron et monodromie', §12 on semistable curves, and it was presumably reused as scrap paper. The header 'XI' is the mirrored 'IX'.

The mathematics, in modern terms:
- **Setup.** X → S is a semistable curve over a henselian trait (or more generally a local base). Its special fibre X_o has ordinary double points x_λ, indexed by a set L identified with an integer interval [1,r].
- **Universal local model.** One constructs a 'universal' semistable deformation f̲: X̲ → S̲ over a W-scheme S̲ (essentially a formal or henselian base with parameters t_λ). The non-smooth locus D' of f̲ splits into components D'_λ, one through each node x_λ. Their images D_λ in S̲ are the discriminant divisors {t_λ = 0}.
- **Base change (12.8.2).** By construction, X → S is the pullback of f̲ along a suitable W-morphism g: S → S̲.
- **Picard scheme (12.8.3).** One sets P = Pic^0_{X̲/S̲}. Because the special fibre is geometrically reduced of dimension 1, f̲ is cohomologically flat in dimension 0 (EGA III 7.8.1). P is formally smooth because H^2(X_o, O_{X_o}) = 0, since X_o is a curve.
- **Representability.** The text admits that P is representable by a smooth group scheme with connected fibres. It cites an unpublished result of Mumford (via reference [22]), generalized by Raynaud over a trait, and alternatively Artin's general representability by algebraic spaces for f proper, flat and cohomologically flat in dimension 0.

The purpose is to compute the monodromy and Néron-model structure (component groups, Picard–Lefschetz-type pairing) of the Jacobian of a semistable curve via the universal deformation.
errors: No mathematical errors visible. In 'P est formellement lisse sur S' the base should presumably be S̲, since P is defined over S̲. This could be a typo in the typescript or in the machine transcription.
The page is misattributed in context: it is a page of SGA 7 Exp. IX (published 1972), not part of the 1976 PD de Rham notes. Only its blank verso was presumably used.

ideas.modern_name: Versal deformation of nodal curves; boundary divisors

ideas.what: Pic^0 of a flat proper curve with reduced fibres: cohomological flatness, formal smoothness via H^2(O)=0, representability (Mumford/Raynaud/Artin)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a recycled typescript page of the published SGA 7 Exposé IX, with standard and well-known content.
transcription_corrections: The page is printed upside down. It is p.160 of Exposé IX of SGA 7 (the header 'XI' is 'IX' mirrored).
'il s'ensuit que F̲ est cohomologiquement plat' should read 'f̲ est cohomologiquement plat'.
'P [-est-] est formellement lisse' reflects a crossed-out duplicate 'est' in the typescript.
There is an illegible handwritten, upside-down marginal note near the top edge. Separately, archive numbering '301' and '478' appears on the page.
